question: Should OpenClaw adopt these three external-verification approval APIs and their durable approval-attempt storage as a supported plugin SDK contract, including the proposed deprecation window for the ignored hook `pluginId` field?
rationale: The patch is a coherent implementation of the linked RFC, but accepting a new public plugin authorization surface and retained compatibility field is a product and long-term API ownership choice that cannot be settled by tests alone.

options.title: Sponsor the API contract
options.body: Accept the RFC-shaped plugin approval surface, require a rebase, and record the compatibility and deprecation lifecycle before merge.

options.title: Narrow before adoption
options.body: Ask for a smaller internal seam or experimental owner-plugin path if maintainers do not want the grant store and verifier APIs to become public SDK commitments.

options.title: Defer the capability
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and pause this implementation until a maintainer explicitly sponsors the plugin API direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the API contract
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC-shaped plugin approval surface, require a rebase, and record the compatibility and deprecation lifecycle before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed domain contact in the supplied PR and canonical-issue history; a repository maintainer must make the final sponsorship decision.
